home.heroSubtitle: Live courses for adults and children — from Ancient Greece to Medieval Russia. Learn to think deeper, question more, and see the past anew.
home.manifestoTitle: A quiet library in the middle of a forest
home.manifesto: We believe history and philosophy are not luxuries but essential tools for understanding ourselves and the world. Our classes are a slow, attentive reading of the past among kindred spirits: no rush, no shallowness, with respect for the sources and for your questions.
home.featuredSubtitle: Enrollment is open — join the next cohorts
home.why1Text: Each course is crafted and taught by a passionate historian and philosopher with years of teaching experience.
home.why2Text: Separate groups for adults, teens and children — everyone explores history and ideas at their own level.
home.why3Text: Classes happen live on Zoom, with questions and discussion. Recordings are yours to keep.
home.why4Text: Every group has its own private Telegram channel with materials, recordings and lively discussion between classes.
home.how1Title: Choose a course and a group
home.how1Text: Each course runs 2–3 months in several groups — pick the day and time that suit you.
home.how2Text: Monthly billing through a secure payment page. No hidden fees.
home.how3Text: Right after payment you automatically receive a personal invite to your group's private channel.
home.how4Text: We meet on Zoom every week. Missed a class? The recording is already waiting in the channel.
home.testimonial1: These aren't lectures — they're journeys. After the Ancient Greece course I went to Athens and saw the city with completely different eyes.
home.testimonial2: My son looks forward to class all week. I've never seen a child so absorbed in history.
home.testimonial3: Philosophy turned out to be a practice, not an abstraction. The Stoics are with me every day now.
home.newsletterText: Once a month — new courses, open lectures and the best books. No spam.

about.title: About the school
about.intro: Inverted Forest is an online school of history and philosophy for Russian-speaking students around the world.
about.story1: Inverted Forest began with a simple idea: serious humanities education can be alive, accessible and engaging — without dumbing down and without academic dryness.
about.story2: Today it is a school offering courses in history, philosophy, literature and anthropology, where adults, teens and children study in small groups, read primary sources and learn to ask questions.
about.story3: The name refers to an inverted forest — a literary image of trees whose roots reach for the sky: knowledge grows from the depths of the past and nourishes the present.
about.value1Text: We read primary sources and serious literature, but we speak a human language.
about.value2Text: Up to 15 people per group — so everyone has a voice and every question is heard.
about.value3Text: Learning doesn't end with the bell: discussions continue in the groups' Telegram channels.
about.ctaText: Choose a course and become part of our forest.

faq.title: Questions & Answers
faq.intro: Everything people usually ask before joining a course.

items.a: Classes are held live on Zoom or Google Meet, once a week, 60–90 minutes. These are not pre-recorded lectures: you can ask questions and join the discussion.

items.q: What if I miss a class?
items.a: All sessions are recorded. Recordings are posted in your group's private Telegram channel within 24 hours and stay available until the end of the course.

Billing is monthly: you pay for a month of study, not for the whole course upfront. Payment is by card on our payment provider's secure page — we never receive or store your card details. Cancellation terms are set out in our Terms and Conditions.

items.q: How do I get access to the group's Telegram channel?
items.a: Automatically: right after payment, a personal one-time invite link arrives by email. The link is valid for 7 days and works only once.

items.q: What language are classes taught in?
items.a: The main language of instruction is Russian. Selected groups and materials are available in English — this is indicated on the course page.

items.q: Is the course suitable for my child?
items.a: We run separate children's and teens' groups with an adapted programme. Age groups are listed on each course page.

items.q: Do I need any prior knowledge?
items.a: No. Every course is designed to be engaging both for newcomers and for those already familiar with the subject. All you need is curiosity and a willingness to read.

items.q: Can I cancel and get a refund?
items.a: Cancellation and refunds are governed by the Israeli Consumer Protection Law and are set out in full in the “Cancellation and Refund Policy” section of our Terms and Conditions. If you have questions, write to us and we'll walk you through it.
